text:
Ben C: quick heads-up — we're prepping a Karpenter roll for GPU pools next week. goal: consolidate old nodepools, enable provisioner-based scaling, and add a warmup pool for scale-to-zero cases. thinking of doing a staged canary across us-west-2 then eu-west-1.

Alice M: nice. main concern is ENI/IP limits and burst launches — last time we hit soft-failures during model training jobs. do we have safe fallback if ENI quota blocks new nodes? :thinking_face:

Dan S: ENI limits are the big one. current per-subnet IPs used = ~82% in us-west-2-gpu-subnet. we can either: (1) route burst pods to on-demand fallback ASG, (2) pre-warm IPs via secondary subnets, or (3) use node consolidation to free IPs by evicting low-priority jobs.

InfraBot: Incident detected: subnet us-west-2-gpu-subnet approaching Elastic IP allocation threshold (82%). Recommend throttling large batch job submissions.

Carla R: +1 for warm pool. proposal: maintain a small warmpool (2-4 gpus) per AZ pinned to same AMI, keep it untainted so latency-sensitive jobs can use it. scale-to-zero idle period = 10m. That reduces cold-start p50 by ~600ms in our test.

Eva L: also add a fallback provisioner config that prefers cheaper spot instances but falls back to on-demand within 90s if spot not available. we should test spot interruption patterns — last month spot preempts increased from 0.8% -> 3.4% during regional maintenance.

Ben C: can someone draft the canary plan? want small % of traffic (5%) on new provisioner for 48h then 25% then full. watch: latency, 95/99, GPU utilization, and error rates. cost delta target: <8% change.

Frank P: putting a quick provisioner snippet for the canary. we'll mount taints for low-priority batch pods.

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-canary
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: kubernetes.io/arch
      operator: In
      values: [amd64]
    - key: accelerator.openai.com/gpu
      operator: Exists
  provider:
    instanceProfile: gpu-node-profile
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 3600
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  labels:
    redwood.k8s/role: gpu-canary
  taints:
    - key: workload
      value: batch
      effect: PreferNoSchedule
```

Dan S: quick note on consolidation: enable consolidation but keep eviction thresholds conservative for the first week (cpu < 10% && gpu-util < 15% for 15m). otherwise we risk noisy evictions affecting training checkpoints.

Alice M: what about node template drift? we still have older nodepools with older AMIs and kubelet flags. migration should include an AMI parity check and kubelet flag audit. can we add a script to fail the canary if drift > 5%?

Frank P: sure — I'll add a CI job that scans node labels/annotations and compares AMI IDs. simple command:

```
kubectl get nodes -l redwood.k8s/role=gpu -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.spec.providerID}\n{end}'
```

fail if any providerID contains the legacy-ami tag.

Carla R: ops playbook for ENI exhaustion: (1) pause batch queue, (2) flip routing to on-demand fallback provisioner, (3) scale warmpool in adjacent AZ, (4) notify infra #pager. doc snippet posted to runbook later. :white_check_mark:

Eva L: metric checklist for canary: node launch latency, pod pending time, evictions, ENI allocation failures (cloud provider metric), spot interrupt count, cost per GPU-hour. push to prometheus and dashboard in console.

Ben C: timeline: draft config + runbook by EOD tomorrow, smoke test today in staging, canary start Monday 09:00 PT. owners: Frank (provisioner YAML + CI), Alice (drift audit), Carla (warmpool + runbook), Dan (ENI fallbacks + monitoring). I'll file a short RFC after this thread.

InfraBot: Deploy job queued: staging/gpu-canary -> started. job id = deploy-20250301-73a9.

Frank P: I'll start the CI job now and post logs if anything breaks.

Alice M: thanks — if anyone sees ENI errors once canary starts, ping me and I'll trigger fallback. :rocket:
